landing.story_text_1: Aristotle walked as he taught. He believed the act of moving — through space, through questions, through observation — was itself a form of thinking. Two thousand years later, the research agrees.
landing.story_text_2: Peripateticware puts that insight in your pocket. Teachers design activities that bring curriculum to life in the real world. Students explore, capture, and reflect. Peri guides the inquiry. And learning — finally — moves.
landing.field_journal_title: The Field Journal: Learning That Stays
landing.field_journal_desc: Students don't just do an activity — they record it. The Field Journal is where raw observations become structured knowledge. Back at their desk, students expand their notes with extended analysis, personal reflection, and connections to what they already know. Teachers can review, respond, and promote entries to the student's permanent portfolio.
landing.field_journal_feature_1: Capture in the field — photo, audio, and written notes geotagged to the exact spot
landing.field_journal_feature_2: Expand at your desk — four structured sections (Analysis, Reflection, Connections, Questions) guide deeper thinking after the activity
landing.field_journal_feature_3: Teacher feedback built in — teachers annotate and approve entries; approved notes flow automatically into the portfolio
landing.your_data_is_yours_we_collect_minimal_in: Your data is yours. We collect minimal information and never sell it. Peripateticware uses encrypted connections, anonymous aggregation, and transparent data practices. You control what data is shared, with whom, and for how long.

student.headline: Learning Happens Outside
student.intro: Explore the world around you, capture what you find, and build a portfolio of real-world discoveries — guided by Peri, your AI inquiry companion.
student.coach_prompt: What do the cattails have that helps them survive here?
student.feature_1_desc: Photo, audio, sketches, and field notes — everything in one place, synced to your portfolio.
student.feature_2_desc: Peri the crow asks the right questions to help you think deeper — sparking ideas, never giving away answers.
student.feature_3_desc: Watch your competencies grow as you complete activities and build your outdoor learning portfolio.
student.feature_4_desc: A multi-step scavenger hunt gives you a live map with an arrow to the next stop and how far it is. Your phone works out when you have arrived — you just walk and look.
student.feature_5_title: Your Location Stays on Your Phone
student.feature_5_desc: On a hunt, nothing about where you are leaves your device — it only records which stop you reached. Anything more is your family's choice, and you still get a working hunt either way.

teacher.headline: Design Activities That Move
teacher.intro: Build geo-tagged, curriculum-aligned outdoor activities in minutes. Students capture evidence in the field, you get real-time progress — no app download required.
teacher.coach_prompt: 3 students submitted evidence · 2 reflections pending review
teacher.feature_1_desc: Design outdoor activities with map-based location selection, Bloom's levels, and AI-suggested inquiry prompts.
teacher.feature_2_desc: See where each student is in real time — which phase they're on, what they've captured, and who needs support.
teacher.feature_3_desc: Competency tracking, portfolio review, and curriculum alignment — all without extra marking time.
teacher.feature_4_title: Build a Route, Not Just a Pin
teacher.feature_4_desc: Drop stops on the map or import a GPX from Gaia GPS, AllTrails, or CalTopo. Give each stop a clue, an arrival radius, and a photo or note prompt — then export the finished hunt as GPX. Build one on your phone in the field, or in the web builder.
teacher.feature_5_desc: Every hunt has a capability ceiling you choose — on-device navigation only, up to geo-tagged evidence — each step a separate, plain-language consent shown to families before the activity starts.

parent.headline: Stay Connected to Their Learning
parent.intro: See what your child is discovering in the field. Receive digest updates, view their evidence portfolio, and celebrate every milestone.
parent.coach_prompt: Maya completed Riparian Biodiversity · 3 captures · 1 reflection
parent.feature_1_desc: Photos, sketches, and field notes from every activity — a real record of your child's outdoor learning.
parent.feature_2_desc: A clear summary of what they explored, what they captured, and how their competencies are growing.
parent.feature_3_desc: Receive updates when activities are completed and milestones are reached — without interrupting class.
parent.feature_4_desc: Every location setting is opt-in and off by default, described in plain words, with how long it's kept shown before you decide. Turn everything off and your child still gets a fully working map hunt — navigation happens on their device.
parent.feature_5_title: Kept Only as Long as It's Useful
parent.feature_5_desc: An exact spot on a submitted photo blurs to about a city block after 30 days. A live position on a field trip is deleted a week after it ends. A recorded path is gone in 30 days — or the moment you ask.

1.desc: Peri sets the scene and asks your child what they notice. No right answer yet — just looking.

2.desc: Your child records what they see, hear, or measure. Peri prompts for specifics if the answer is vague.

3.desc: Peri asks comparison and classification questions. What\'s similar? What\'s different? What pattern do you see?

4.desc: Your child proposes a cause or mechanism. Peri tests it with evidence questions, not hints.

5.desc: Peri asks what this means for a new situation. Knowledge becomes portable.

1.text: You\'re at the creek bank. Before we measure anything — what\'s the first thing you notice about the water right here versus ten feet upstream?

2.text: It\'s slower here and there\'s more mud on the bottom.

3.text: Good observation. Why do you think the mud settled here and not upstream where the water is faster?

4.text: Maybe slower water can\'t carry as much stuff?

5.text: That\'s the right direction. What could you measure or photograph here to support that idea?

homeschool.headline: Your Classroom. Your Backyard. Your Rules.
homeschool.intro: Peripateticware gives homeschool families a complete learning platform — create activities for any location, track each child\'s progress against state standards, and generate portfolio reports automatically.
homeschool.feature_1_desc: Build activities tied to real places — nature trails, museums, historical sites, or your own backyard. Each child follows guided prompts and captures evidence on their device.
homeschool.feature_2_desc: Upload your state\'s reporting requirements and automatically track coverage as your children complete activities. Know exactly what\'s met, what\'s partial, and what\'s missing.
homeschool.feature_3_desc: Generate PDF portfolio reports and activity log CSVs for state filings or your own records — no manual spreadsheets required.
homeschool.feature_4_title: Turn a Trail Into a Hunt
homeschool.feature_4_desc: Walk your route and drop each stop where you stand, right from your phone — or import a GPX track from a hiking app. Your learners follow a map with live distance to the next stop, resolved on the device.
homeschool.feature_5_desc: You are both the guardian and the teacher, so you approve any location sharing yourself, per activity — no separate parent-consent round trip, and everything defaults to the private, on-device option.

landing.homeschool_section_desc: Peripateticware treats homeschool parents as both teacher and parent in one account. You own your children\'s accounts directly — no link codes, no bureaucracy.
landing.hs_feat_children_desc: Create accounts for each child directly from your dashboard. Set their grade level and age band (K–2, 3–6, 7–12) so activities and Peri\'s guidance adapt to them automatically.
landing.hs_feat_activities_desc: Use the full teacher activity builder to create learning experiences tied to real places. A nature trail, a museum, a historical marker in your town — anywhere becomes a classroom.
landing.hs_feat_standards_desc: Upload your state\'s homeschool reporting requirements as a PDF or CSV. Peripateticware\'s AI extracts each criterion so you can review and save them without manual data entry.
landing.hs_feat_coverage_desc: See exactly which requirements are met, partially met, or not yet covered — broken down by child and subject. Know your gaps before your annual review.
landing.hs_feat_portfolio_desc: Generate a polished PDF portfolio with cover page, activity log, evidence thumbnails, and standards coverage summary. CSV export available for states that want a spreadsheet.
landing.hs_feat_ai_desc: Peri — the crow mascot — guides each child through activities with Aristotelian inquiry questions adapted to their age band and Bloom\'s taxonomy level. Socratic learning, built in.
landing.hs_step_1: Create your homeschool account and add each child
landing.hs_step_3: Build activities tied to real locations and subjects
landing.hs_step_4: Children complete activities; evidence is captured automatically
landing.hs_step_5: Export your portfolio or coverage report at any time

pages_originstorypage.from_a_white_paper_to_a_working_platform: From a White Paper to a Working Platform: Peripateticware 2007–2026
pages_originstorypage.the_paper_was_written_at_a_moment_when_3: The paper was written at a moment when 3G hadn't fully rolled out, the iPhone was months away from launch, and "app" wasn't yet a common word. Its predictions — that cell phones would become 1-for-1 classroom devices, that mobile networks would reach remote regions, that GPS would become cheap enough to put in every student's pocket — all came true. The products the paper called for did not.
pages_originstorypage.the_2007_document_named_one_obstacle_it_: The 2007 document named one obstacle it couldn't solve:
pages_originstorypage.if_students_follow_their_curiosity_throu: If students follow their curiosity through real places, learning about arches, barrels, and celestial navigation because they're standing near a cathedral or a harbour, how do you assess what they've learned in a way that satisfies curriculum requirements? How do you produce the spreadsheet of numbers the principal wants while also honouring the complexity of what the student actually understood?
pages_originstorypage.the_document_left_that_question_open_the: The document left that question open. The school system didn't solve it either. For nearly two decades, "outdoor learning" remained either a vague aspiration or a logistical nightmare — teachers with clipboards, activities that produced no artifact, experiences that disappeared the moment students came back inside.
pages_originstorypage.the_2026_answer_ai_did_what_spreadsheets: The 2026 Answer: AI Did What Spreadsheets Couldn't
pages_originstorypage.the_assessment_problem_turned_out_to_hav: The assessment problem turned out to have two parts. The first was capturing evidence — what did the student actually observe, and can you prove it? The second was evaluating it — did their thinking deepen, or did they just describe what they saw?
pages_originstorypage.the_first_part_was_solved_by_smartphones: The first part was solved by smartphones. Photo, audio, GPS coordinates, timestamps — a student at a creek bank can capture more evidence in ten minutes than a field trip clipboard could hold in a day. What remained was the second part: structured inquiry that didn't just document experience but deepened it.
pages_originstorypage.thats_where_peri_comes_in_peri_is_peripa: That's where Peri comes in. Peri is Peripateticware's AI guide — named, like the software, after the Aristotelian method. Peri doesn't answer questions. It asks them. It follows the five-phase inquiry sequence — Engage, Observe, Analyse, Explain, Apply — that Aristotle used in the Lyceum and that cognitive science has since validated as a path to genuine understanding, not just retention. Peri takes a student's observation and asks the next right question. When the student gets it right, Peri tests the implication. When the student is vague, Peri asks for evidence.
pages_originstorypage.the_result_is_an_artifact_a_field_journa: The result is an artifact: a field journal entry with captures, extended analysis, and a record of the inquiry itself. Teachers can see not just what a student concluded but how they got there. Rubrics aligned to Bloom's taxonomy and standards frameworks — CCSS, NGSS, TEKS, or your own — make the assessment legible to any curriculum coordinator. The spreadsheet and the real learning finally occupy the same document.
pages_originstorypage.the_2007_paper_described_a_choose_your_o: The 2007 paper described a "choose your own adventure" model of learning — one where students follow tangents, pursue what interests them, and encounter core curriculum concepts through the side doors of genuine curiosity rather than the front door of instruction. The paper acknowledged this was "somewhat chaotic" and that it would require new kinds of instructional design, new assessment tools, and teachers willing to trade some control for authentic engagement.
pages_originstorypage.peripateticware_doesnt_fully_solve_the_c: Peripateticware doesn\'t fully solve the chaos — that tension is real and probably permanent. What it does is give teachers enough structure to stay sane (designed activities, learning targets, completion phases, teacher approval workflows) while giving students enough freedom to actually go somewhere (GPS-triggered content, student-proposed activities, self-directed field notes, peer projects).
pages_originstorypage.the_reverse_scavenger_hunt_where_student: The reverse scavenger hunt — where students propose an activity based on something they found — is the closest thing in the platform to that 2007 vision. A student finds a peculiar rock formation. They propose it as an activity. The teacher approves it. Other students go look. Questions emerge that no curriculum document anticipated. Learning moves.
pages_originstorypage.the_short_answer_is_that_most_of_the_ena: The short answer is that most of the enabling technology wasn\'t ready in 2007. GPS in every pocket came first (2010–2015). Then high-quality mobile cameras. Then cloud APIs cheap enough for schools. Then local AI models (Ollama, llama.cpp) that can run on a teacher\'s home server without a $10,000/month inference bill. The 2007 paper was right about the destination; it couldn\'t have known how long the road would be.
pages_originstorypage.the_longer_answer_is_that_educational_te: The longer answer is that educational technology spent those years solving the wrong problem. EdTech iterated on the classroom — better LMS, better video, better quiz tools. It made the existing model more efficient. Peripateticware doesn\'t try to make the classroom more efficient. It tries to replace the classroom, at least occasionally, with the world.
pages_originstorypage.thats_a_harder_sell_schools_are_riskaver: That\'s a harder sell. Schools are risk-averse. Outdoor learning has a liability optic. "The world is your classroom" sounds like a marketing line until you\'ve watched a ten-year-old explain sediment transport to a crow-shaped AI guide while standing in a creek bed, and then read the field journal entry they wrote that afternoon, and understood that they understood.
